video.subject_count.evidence: [director·claude] I counted the people in all 104 cells, from 00:00:00.000 to 00:00:25.750. Every cell has the same single woman sitting on the edge of the bed in the centre of the frame. Her dark wavy long hair and beige short-sleeved shirt stay the same throughout. No one is added or removed, and there is no duplicate of her. The two gesture beats (4.75–5.75 s, thumb pointing behind her; 12.25–13.25 s, palm spread) also show only her.

video.no_text.evidence: [director·claude·审稿兜底，待机检工具] Apart from the yellow timecode added by the review tool in each cell's top-left corner, no cell has subtitles, a watermark, a logo or UI. The plaster wall at upper left shows only mottled warm texture and no letter-like marks. The window opening at upper right shows only cool blue night.

video.object_continuity.evidence: [director·claude] The oil lamp on the stool in the bottom-left corner is lit and stays in the same place in every cell from 0.000 to 25.750 s. It does not move, go out or vanish. The window opening at upper right and the dark blanket on the bed stay put in every cell. The right thumb points over her shoulder at 4.75–5.75 s, and her hands are back on her knees by 6.0 s. The left palm spreads toward frame right at 12.25–13.25 s, and her hands are back on her knees by 13.5 s. Both moves start and end at the knees. No objects appear from nowhere, float or pass through anything.

video.person_still.evidence: [director·claude·审稿兜底，待机检工具] 0.000–0.750 s: she holds her head turned toward the wall at upper left with a slight change of pose. This is the silent 0–1 s beat in the shot plan, where she looks back at the scratches, and it lasts under 1.5 s. 1.0–2.0 s: she turns her face back to the camera. 2.25–23.75 s: her mouth shape changes between neighbouring cells, her head tilts slightly, and the two gestures (4.75 s and 12.25 s) run continuously, so she never sits frozen like a prop. 24.0–25.75 s: she smiles, and her head drops to look down toward the lamp at 25.5–25.75 s. That is the quiet beat in the shot plan, and she is still moving.

video.acting_natural.evidence: [Riley·claude] With the sound off, the shot shows Riley sitting on the edge of the bed by lamplight. She first glances back at the scratches on the wall, then turns to the camera and talks gently, points at the wall once and opens a hand toward the room once, and ends by smiling and looking down at the lamp. That matches the point of the shot: guests writing on the walls was everyday life, and she is calmly retelling a sweet line. Beat by beat from the sheet: 0.000–1.000s her head is turned toward frame left and up at the scratches behind her, mouth closed and smiling, hands on her knees. 1.250–1.750s she turns her face back gradually, a natural lead-in. 2.000–4.500s she faces the camera and speaks, hands still on her knees. 4.750–5.500s she raises her right hand near her right shoulder and points back at the wall, mouth open as she speaks; the gesture is about the size of the line, not bigger. By 5.750–6.000s the hand is back on her knee. 6.000–12.000s she keeps talking to the camera, hands relaxed on her knees, upper body and head shifting slightly between cells, not frozen. 12.250–13.250s she opens her left hand palm-up toward frame right (into the room) and her eyes follow it (12.250–12.500s); by 12.750s she is looking at the camera again, and by 13.500s her hand is back on her knee. That is cause and effect, with no lag. 13.750–21.750s she speaks steadily with her hands still and her expression shifting with the words. No gesture or expression repeats, and nothing is overplayed. 22.000–23.750s she smiles after the line, which fits the size of 'That's kind of sweet'. 24.000–25.750s she stops talking, her head gradually dips, and her eyes drop toward the lamp at frame left (clearest at 25.500–25.750s), a quiet ending. Throughout she addresses the camera, as she should. She never stiffens like a prop, no beat drags, and no reaction lags more than 1.5s. Her eyebrow raise at 'history textbook' is too small to see on the sheet and was not used in this judgment.

video.point_landed.evidence: [director·claude] What I see with the sound off: at night, in a small ancient room lit only by an oil lamp, a woman sits on the bed. At 0–0.75 s she turns back and looks at the wall at upper left, smiling. From 2 s she talks to the camera. At 4.75–5.5 s she points her thumb over her shoulder at the wall behind her. At 12.25–13.25 s her palm spreads toward the room. At 25.5 s she looks down at the lamp and smiles. From this I can tell she is talking about the wall behind her and the room. The point depends on there being visible 'messages left by guests' on that wall. In every cell the wall at upper left is about 250 px wide, and I can only make out mottled warm plaster. I cannot tell whether the darker patch of messy scratches above the lamp, or the faint scratches covering the wall, are actually there. So I cannot judge whether, with the sound off, the shot reads as 'guests leave messages on the walls.' The parts I can check are fine: the lamp is the only warm light source, the window adds cool blue, and the two gestures each take about 0.75–1 s, which is a natural human speed.
